title: Forces: Frictional, Gravitational, and Elastic Spring Force (Advanced)
subject: Science

questions.question: Which of the following scenarios describes an interaction where ONLY a pulling force is being applied to the object?
options: A footballer kicking a stationary ball across the field
A student using a magnet to pick up steel paperclips
A baker kneading dough on a wooden board
A carpenter hammering a nail into a piece of wood
questions.explanation: Magnetic force acts as a pull in this context, drawing the paperclips toward the magnet. Kicking, kneading, and hammering involve pushing forces.

questions.question: Two boys are pushing a heavy crate in opposite directions. The crate remains stationary. Which statement is correct?
options: There are no forces acting on the crate
The forces applied by both boys are equal in strength
The frictional force is greater than the pushing forces
The crate has too much mass for gravity to move it
questions.explanation: If the crate does not move, the forces are balanced. This shows that a force can move a stationary object only if the applied force is greater than the opposing forces like friction.

questions.question: A parachutist falls at a constant speed after opening his parachute. What is the effect of the forces acting on him?
options: The force of gravity has stopped acting on him
Air resistance is now acting in the same direction as gravity
The upward force of air resistance balances the downward force of gravity
The force of gravity is now weaker than the air resistance
questions.explanation: While gravity pulls him down, air resistance (a form of friction) pushes up. When these forces balance, his speed remains constant rather than increasing.

questions.question: A student tests four different springs by hanging a 200g weight on each. Which spring exerts the GREATEST elastic spring force to resist the weight?
options: Spring A: Extended by 10cm
Spring B: Extended by 2cm
Spring C: Extended by 5cm
Spring D: Extended by 8cm
questions.explanation: Spring B is the 'stiffest' because it stretched the least under the same load. It exerts a stronger elastic spring force to maintain its shape compared to the others.

questions.question: An astronaut travels from Earth to Jupiter, where gravity is much stronger. How do his mass and weight change?
options: His mass increases, but his weight stays the same
Both his mass and weight increase
His mass stays the same, but his weight increases
His mass stays the same, but his weight decreases
questions.explanation: Mass is the amount of matter and does not change with location. Weight is the measure of gravitational force; since Jupiter's gravity is stronger, his weight increases.

questions.question: A block is pulled across a table. Why does it require more force to start the block moving than to keep it moving?
options: Gravity only acts on the block when it is stationary
Frictional force is strongest when the surfaces are first resisting motion
The block's mass increases when it is at rest
The elastic spring force of the table pushes against the block
questions.explanation: Friction opposes motion. More force is needed to overcome the initial friction between the two surfaces to move a stationary object.

questions.question: When a spring is compressed between two hands, which of the following is an effect of the force applied by the hands?
options: The mass of the spring decreases
The spring's gravitational force increases
The shape of the spring is changed
The spring becomes a magnet
questions.explanation: One effect of a force is to change the shape of an object. When you push on both ends of the spring, it becomes shorter – its shape has been changed by the applied force.

questions.question: Which of these factors does NOT affect the amount of frictional force between a sliding wooden block and the floor?
options: The roughness of the floor surface
The mass of the wooden block
The surface area of the block in contact with the floor
The presence of a lubricant like oil on the floor
questions.explanation: In most standard science investigations, friction depends on the nature of the surfaces and the weight of the object, not the size of the contact area.

questions.question: Why would a person weigh less on the peak of Mount Everest than at sea level?
options: There is less air pressure at the peak
The person has less mass at higher altitudes
The person is further from the Earth's center, so gravitational force is slightly weaker
The cold temperature reduces the elastic spring force in the body
questions.explanation: Weight is the measure of gravitational force. As distance from the center of the Earth increases, the pull of gravity decreases slightly.

questions.question: In a rainy climate, why do some stairs have thin strips of sandpaper glued to the edges?
options: To reduce the weight of the stairs
To increase friction and prevent slipping when the surface is wet
To absorb excess gravitational force
To make the stairs change shape more easily
questions.explanation: Water acts as a lubricant and reduces friction. Sandpaper provides a rougher surface to increase friction, allowing for better grip.

questions.question: A ball is thrown horizontally. Which force eventually causes it to hit the ground?
options: The force of the throw
Air resistance
Magnetic force
Gravitational force
questions.explanation: While the throw moves it forward, gravitational force acts continuously to pull the ball downward toward the center of the Earth.

questions.question: Which of the following would be the most effective way to INCREASE the distance a toy car travels after being pushed?
options: Using a rougher surface like a carpet
Adding more weight to the toy car
Applying a lubricant to the wheels' axles
Using square-shaped wheels
questions.explanation: Lubricants reduce unwanted friction between moving parts, allowing the wheels to spin more freely and the car to travel further.

questions.question: A book is placed on a table. The book does not move. Which statement correctly describes the forces acting on the book?
options: Only gravity acts on the book
The table pushes upward on the book with a force equal to the book's weight
The book's weight is greater than the force from the table
No forces act on the book because it is not moving
questions.explanation: Two forces act on the stationary book: gravity pulls it downward, and the table pushes upward with an equal force. These balanced forces result in no movement.

questions.question: A spring has an original length of 15cm. When a 50g weight is added, it becomes 17cm. What will the total length be if the weight is increased to 150g?
options: 19cm
21cm
22cm
45cm
questions.explanation: The extension for 50g is 2cm (17 - 15). For 150g (3 times the weight), the extension will be 6cm (2 x 3). Total length = 15cm + 6cm = 21cm.

questions.question: Why is it more difficult to stop a heavy truck than a small car moving at the same speed?
options: The truck has more mass, requiring a larger force to change its motion
The truck has less friction with the road
Gravity pulls the car harder because it is closer to the ground
The car has more elastic spring force in its brakes
questions.explanation: Objects with more mass require a greater force to change their speed or stop their motion.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about all forces?
options: They can only be seen when something moves
They are always beneficial to machines
They can act from a distance without touching the object
They always cause an object to speed up
questions.explanation: Non-contact forces like gravity and magnetic force can act on an object without physical contact.

questions.question: A student wants to investigate the effect of mass on the friction of a sled. She uses four sleds with different masses but the same base material. What must she keep constant?
options: The mass of the sleds
The type of surface the sleds slide on
The amount of force used to pull the sleds
The speed at which she pulls the sleds
questions.explanation: In a fair test, only the variable being tested (mass) should change. The surface must stay the same to see how mass alone affects friction.

questions.question:
A student used a spring balance to pull a block across four surfaces. The results are shown below:
Surface W: 2.5N
Surface X: 1.2N
Surface Y: 4.0N
Surface Z: 0.5N
Which surface would be best for a 'slip-and-slide' water toy?
options: Surface W
Surface X
Surface Y
Surface Z
questions.explanation: Surface Z required the least force to move the block, meaning it has the lowest frictional force. This makes it the most 'slippery'.

questions.question: Which statement accurately describes the relationship between friction and heat?
options: Friction always destroys heat
Heat is a force that creates friction
Frictional force between moving surfaces often produces heat
Friction only works in cold temperatures
questions.explanation: When surfaces rub against each other, the interaction of the particles creates heat. This is why hands feel warm when rubbed together.

questions.question: A student argues that 'Without gravity, we would still have weight but no mass.' Is this correct?
options: Yes, mass depends on gravity
No, we would have mass but no weight
No, we would have neither mass nor weight
Yes, because weight is a constant property of matter
questions.explanation: Mass is the amount of matter in an object and is constant. Weight is the result of gravitational force acting on that mass. Without gravity, there is no weight.
